quote: nor could the matrons be kept at home, either by advice or shame, nor even by the commands of their husbands
notes: Phase 1 of the Lex Oppia repeal struggle at livy:en:34:1: matrons fill the streets and Capitol to press for repeal of the sumptuary law while two tribunes threaten veto.

quote: the women next day poured out into public in much greater numbers, and in a body beset the doors of the tribunes
notes: Phase 2 at livy:en:34:8: after the Cato-Valerius debate the matrons escalate, blockading the houses of the vetoing tribunes until they yield.

quote: nor did they retire until this intervention was withdrawn
notes: Resolution phase at livy:en:34:8: the Bruti withdraw their tribunician veto under crowd pressure and all tribes vote the Oppian law's repeal, twenty years after enactment.

quote: procured men who were to set fire by night to several parts of the city at once
notes: At livy:en:34:44 the imprisoned Pleminius plots nocturnal arson across Rome to cover a prison break; accomplices inform, the senate is told, and he is summarily put to death in the lower dungeon.

quote: they ordered the curule aediles to set apart places for the senators, distinct from those of the people
notes: At livy:en:34:44 the censors institute segregated senatorial seating at the Roman games, ending promiscuous seating and winning the senate's gratitude.

quote: the senators, for the first time, sat separate from the people, which, as every innovation usually does, gave occasion to various observations
notes: Implementation/controversy phase at livy:en:34:54: first separate senatorial seating at the games divides opinion as an affront to liberty and concord, and Africanus reportedly regrets it.

quote: In this year colonies of Roman citizens were settled at Puteoli, Vulturnum, and Liternum; three hundred men in each place
notes: At livy:en:34:45 citizen colonies are planted at Puteoli, Vulturnum, Liternum, Salernum, Buxentum, Sipontum, Tempsa and Croto on confiscated Campanian and other lands under triumviral commissions.

quote: proposed to the people, and the people ordered, that two Latin colonies should be settled, one in Bruttium
notes: At livy:en:34:53 the tribune Tubero, on a senate decree, carries a plebiscite founding two Latin colonies in Bruttium and the Thurine territory, with three-year commissioners elected in the Capitol.

quote: made application to the plebeian tribunes, to take cognizance of the cases of such men as claimed exemption from the service
notes: At livy:en:34:56 soldiers resist the Ligurian emergency levy by appealing to the tribunes for exemptions until the senate votes a Gallic tumultus, barring tribunician cognizance of the claims.

quote: the consuls, by direction of the senate, published an edict, that, on any day whereon religious rites should be ordered
notes: At livy:en:34:55 incessant earthquake reports paralyze public business until, after a three-day supplication, the consuls' edict forbids reporting a new earthquake on a day already under expiatory rites.

quote: he settled the iron and silver mines on such a footing, that they produced a large revenue
notes: At livy:en:34:21 Cato institutes a new fiscal regime for the Spanish iron and silver mines, a provincial-revenue reform credited with enriching the province; marginal as a domestic event.

quote: laid claim to a privilege unheard of before; that Latins, giving in their names for a Roman colony, should be deemed citizens of Rome
notes: At livy:en:34:42 Ferentinate Latins enrolled for citizen colonies claim Roman citizenship, an unprecedented privilege the senate rejects; coded as an attempted (failed) institutional innovation.
